header.name: Jeremy Jerome Chia
header.tagline: Lecturer and Analytics Practitioner — Business Analytics and Data

summary: Analytics practitioner and instructor with 6+ years building finance data systems at scale across APAC and Europe, 3 years designing and delivering data analytics curriculum in Berlin (80% class progression vs. 50% school average), and 2 years as Teaching Assistant at NTU across three 45-student seminar groups. Combines subject matter depth in business analytics, statistical modelling, and data engineering with hands-on curriculum design, assessment grading, and one-on-one student support. MSc in Big Data and Business Analytics (ESCP, Valedictorian) and peer-reviewed publications in applied analytics and NLP. Permanent Resident, Germany — no visa sponsorship required.
teachingPhilosophy: The real obstacle in analytics education is rarely mathematical: students freeze not because they misunderstand a confidence interval or decision tree, but because they do not yet trust themselves to act on uncertain, quantified information. The goal of every course is a specific transformation — from 'I do not know how to approach this' to 'I know how to approach this' — and staying connected with students long enough to see that confidence carry forward. Courses are structured around frameworks and concepts rather than tools, so the foundation outlasts the next wave of software change. Direct instruction for deterministic content; inquiry-based seminars for applied, judgement-heavy questions where reasonable people working from the same data can legitimately reach different recommendations.
